claims.text: HfNbTaTiZr is a single-phase, disordered BCC or similar refractory high-entropy alloy.
The random distribution of atoms with different radii produces significant lattice distortion and variations in interatomic distances in HfNbTaTiZr.
Severe lattice distortion creates heterogeneous local bond stiffness and local elastic modulus.
Regions of varying bond strength and elastic modulus hinder ordinary dislocation mobility.
Lattice distortion alters atomic vibrational amplitudes.
Lattice distortion delays or moderates elevated-temperature mechanical softening.
Lattice distortion reduces thermal expansion relative to a more homogeneous lattice.
Lattice distortion causes elastic modulus to decline more gradually with increasing temperature.
Relative to a refractory control alloy with less atomic-size mismatch, HfNbTaTiZr will have a lower thermal expansion coefficient.
Relative to that control, HfNbTaTiZr will exhibit a nonlinear stress-strain response and more sustained yield strength at elevated temperatures.
Relative to that control, the elastic modulus of HfNbTaTiZr will decline more slowly with temperature.
A refractory alloy made from elements with closer atomic radii will possess less lattice distortion and a more uniform lattice.
The proposed effects should persist from room temperature to approximately 900 degrees Celsius.
The proposed effects are limited to regimes without significant phase transformation, recrystallization, or other microstructural change.
Dynamic precipitation or diffusion processes may influence the thermal expansion and elastic responses.
Prior work reports unique elevated-temperature deformation behavior in a refractory high-entropy alloy.
The exact quantitative effect of lattice distortion on thermal expansion and elastic properties is uncertain.
